reason: An automorphism sends each initial ideal (u_1,...,u_{i-1}) to (phi(u_1),...,phi(u_{i-1})) and therefore induces isomorphisms of the corresponding quotients. Under these quotient isomorphisms, the class of u_i maps to the class of phi(u_i), so non-zero-divisorness is preserved in both directions; the optional final nonzero-quotient condition is preserved as well. Degree preservation is immediate from the definition of a graded automorphism.
